method: Completed frame and owner-lifetime stress tests. Explicit Chromium full GC precedes every memory checkpoint. The supplied model remains local.

finding.trigger: A mask-only part with renderWhenUsedAsMask=false never enters the display tree.
finding.cause: Application.destroy traversed only attached children, leaving an unparented owned mesh and its texture alive. The Pixi global Cache retained its HTMLImageElement.
finding.fix: Destroy unparented owned part meshes, including their textures and sources, before Application destruction. Attached meshes retain the existing teardown path.

unitRegression.after: 12 tests passed, including exactly one release across repeated destroy calls

browserRegression.before: failed: 12 extra DOM nodes after 12 lifetimes
browserRegression.after: passed: no accumulation beyond the 2-node bound

finding.integrationIsolation: vitest.memory.config.ts runs GC tests alone; ordinary visual tests exclude *.memory.integration.tsx.

remainingAllocations.interpretation: JS heap is not byte-identical after repeated renderer lifetimes. About 2-3 MiB remained within the predeclared 8 MiB budget; sampled stacks include Pixi shader source identifier tables. The reproduced image/DOM accumulation is fixed. Listener, Worker and WebGL2-context counts remain bounded. This is not a claim that all retained cache bytes disappear.

limits: Chromium JS heap, ArrayBuffer backing storage and Wasm linear-memory capacities are measured separately. GPU-driver VRAM and OS process RSS are not measured.
Frame counts and repeated ownership changes replace a real multi-hour timer soak. Time-based work only triggered after hours was not exercised.
The 13,200-frame Worker and 3,310-notification playback runs preceded the teardown fix. The Worker artifact remains identical; current-artifact lifecycle reruns follow the fix.
Finite tests cannot establish absence of arbitrarily small leaks or behavior on all devices.
